summary: Specifies how to add SNMP MIB object values to IPFIX flow records, so existing MIB definitions can be reused instead of defining new IPFIX fields. It defines two Options Templates and a method to create more.

eli5.summary: Flow reports list who talked to whom. This lets you attach extra facts already defined elsewhere, rather than inventing new labels.

questions: ipfix options templates for mib objects
how to export mib objects in ipfix
what is a mib field options template
how does ipfix export snmp tables
subtitle: How a flow exporter can attach SNMP MIB object values to IPFIX records without defining a new field for each one.

tldr.problem: IPFIX carries flow data and SNMP MIBs describe device data, but joining them meant polling SNMP separately or defining a new IPFIX Information Element for every MIB object. Polled values also arrive at a different time from the flow records.
tldr.mechanism: New mibObjectValue Information Elements carry the value of any MIB object inside an IPFIX Data Record. A MIB Field Options Template and its data records tell the collector which MIB object identifier each field holds.
tldr.outcome: Any existing or future MIB object can ride along with flow data, including whole conceptual rows and tables, and the SNMP and IPFIX data are exported together.

today: RFC 8038 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2017. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why Export MIB Values in IPFIX
sections.content:
IPFIX is a push protocol: an Exporter sends flow data to a Collector. SNMP is a polling protocol whose data is described by Management Information Base (MIB) modules. The two overlap. IPFIX already has elements such as ingressInterface and egressInterface that carry an ifIndex value defined in RFC 2863.

A Collector could poll the Exporter over SNMP to learn more about those interfaces, but the RFC lists three problems. It needs a mediation function between two data models. Checking that a simple mapping such as ifIndex to ifName is still valid means watching for reloads or forcing ifIndex persistence. And counters in flow records and counters polled by SNMP are read at different times, so they cannot be correlated.

The goals are to complement IPFIX Data Records with MIB objects, avoid defining new Information Elements for objects that are already fully specified, allow correlation of SNMP and IPFIX data by exporting them together, and make it easier to bring SNMP-only devices into IPFIX collection systems.

This document does not carry SNMP notifications, and because IPFIX is push-only with no acknowledgment, it cannot be used to execute configuration changes.
sections.eli5: Imagine a report card that lists your classes, and you want to add each teacher's phone number. You could keep calling the school office, but the numbers might change between calls. It is better to print them on the card right next to the grades.

sections.title: The Solution at a Glance
sections.content:
The RFC defines a method for building IPFIX Options Templates that export the extra data needed to describe MIB objects. A Template can then mix ordinary IPFIX Information Elements with MIB Object Identifiers (OIDs), for columnar or non-columnar objects, including enterprise-specific ones.

Three pieces are added to IPFIX:

  • Two standard Options Templates: the MIB Field Options Template and the MIB Type Options Template.
  • Three classes of new Information Elements: the MIB Object Value elements, the MIB Field Options elements and the MIB Type elements.
  • Two new IPFIX semantics, snmpCounter and snmpGauge.

For conceptual rows and tables, the RFC uses IPFIX Structured Data (RFC 6313) to cut down repeated OID and index data. Providing index information for columnar objects is optional, because an Exporter may use the object purely as type information or may not know the indexing.
sections.eli5: The new system is a set of sticker types. Some stickers hold the value, some say which question the value answers, and some give a longer description for people who want it.

sections.title: Mapping MIB Types to Information Elements
sections.content:
The SYNTAX clause of a MIB object defines its data structure. For each possible SYNTAX, the RFC says exactly which mibObjectValue Information Element to use. If the SYNTAX is a textual convention, the definition is consulted to find the base type, which may recurse through other textual conventions. If the SYNTAX uses a textual convention or sub-typing, the mibObjectSyntax element SHOULD be used to tell the Collector.

Values use the normal IPFIX encoding of abstract data types. The one new encoding rule is that Object Identifiers are encoded as ASN.1/BER inside an octetArray. All of these elements are standard IPFIX fields with the enterprise bit set to 0, even when the exported object comes from an enterprise-specific MIB module. The OID itself shows where the object was defined.

Exporting a MIB object value does not imply that the SNMP process on the device supports that MIB module. The Exporting Process may create the data itself, as long as it matches the object definition.
sections.eli5: Each kind of answer, such as a number, a word or an address, gets its own kind of box. You pick the box that matches the answer.

sections.title: MIB Field Options Template and Records
sections.content:
A MIB OID does not fit in a normal IPFIX Template Record, which gives each field only a 16-bit Information Element identifier. Without the OID, the Collector would see fields that all look the same. So the RFC adds a MIB Field Options Template, a standard Options Template whose records annotate the fields of a Data Template.

Three fields are REQUIRED: the scope field templateId, the scope field informationElementIndex (a zero-based index into the Template), and either mibObjectIdentifier or mibSubIdentifier. Together, templateId and the index point to exactly one mibObjectValue field. The OID is sent in ASN.1/BER form and SHOULD use variable-length encoding, signalled by a field length of 65535.

Optional extras include mibCaptureTimeSemantics (recommended for counters and statistics, to say when in the flow's life the value was read), mibIndexIndicator, and the SNMP context fields. A MIB Type Options Template can additionally carry mibObjectName, mibObjectDescription, mibObjectSyntax and mibModuleName, which helps a Collector that has no copy of the MIB module.

The export order is fixed: the Data Template (Set ID 2), the MIB Field Options Template (Set ID 3), the MIB Field Options Data Records (Set ID 256 or above), then the Data Records. The first three MUST be in the same IPFIX Message. A Collector MUST keep the MIB Field Options data for the length of the Transport Session.
sections.eli5: The value box has no label, so a second small note is sent first. The note says that box number 2 in this list means a certain question. The reader then knows what each box holds.

sections.title: Rows, Tables and Indexes
sections.content:
Many MIB objects are columns of a conceptual row, which is found by an index. The RFC gives three ways to export them: ignore the indexing and use the object purely as a data type, export whole rows or tables with IPFIX Structured Data, or export individual indexed columns.

mibObjectValueRow is a subTemplateList that holds one complete or partial row. Its Template MUST be an Options Template, and the INDEX objects MUST be its Scope Fields in the order of the INDEX clause. The OID exported is the row entry (for IF-MIB, ifEntry rather than ifTable). The columns inside need only a mibSubIdentifier: for a row OID of 1.2.3.4.5.6, a sub-identifier of 1 means 1.2.3.4.5.6.1. mibObjectValueTable works the same way but can hold zero or more rows.

Rows that use an AUGMENTS clause have extra rules about which fields may use a sub-identifier and which need their full OID. If several augmenting rows are exported, the base table SHOULD be the main OID.

The alternative is field-based indexing with mibIndexIndicator, a 64-bit flag field in which the n-th least significant bit marks the n-th Information Element of the Data Record as an index. Index fields MUST be in the order the conceptual row defines.
sections.eli5: A table is like a class roster. You can send the whole row for one student at once, or send one grade with a note saying whose grade it is.

sections.title: Contexts, Templates and Collectors
sections.content:
Each MIB OID is looked up in an SNMP context, usually the default one. If a value is not in the default context, the Exporter MUST include mibContextEngineID and mibContextName, either in the MIB Field Options records or in the same Template as the value. Context fields in the Template take precedence, and each engine ID and name pair needs its own Template.

Templates are managed as in RFC 7011, with extra rules. If a Template using a mibObjectValue is resent, the records it depends on MUST be resent. A replacement Template needs a fresh MIB Field Options Data Record. Template IDs of MIB Field Options Templates MUST NOT be reused while Data Templates still need them. Over SCTP, in size-limited environments, the pieces MAY be sent in separate Messages on the same reliable SCTP stream if their order is kept.

A Collector MUST store the OID records with the same retention policy as Templates, SHOULD have access to MIB modules to look up OIDs, and MUST support all three ways of handling columnar objects. It MAY log a warning if it cannot decode an OID. Because reduced-size encoding may be used, a received field size is not necessarily the maximum.
sections.eli5: The note about what each box means must always travel in the same envelope as the box list. If the box list is sent again, the notes are sent again too.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of IPFIX (RFC 7011) apply. If the Exporter creates or captures the values itself and uses MIB objects only as an encoding or type mechanism, nothing more is needed.

If the Exporter acts as an SNMP manager reading from an SNMP agent, it MUST authenticate itself to the agent, and the agent MUST enforce SNMP access control. Which MIB objects are exported is controlled by the Exporter's configuration, so operators should only include objects that the receiving Collector is allowed to see, remembering that several users may have access to Collector data.

For objects considered sensitive, the Exporter should consider anonymization per RFC 6235 where the data can be anonymized.
sections.eli5: If you put extra facts on the report, make sure the people reading it are allowed to see them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned two IPFIX semantics: snmpCounter (value 7) and snmpGauge (value 8). They match the SNMP Counter and Gauge types. Unlike the IPFIX totalCounter semantic, an SNMP counter does not start at 0.

It also allocated 21 new Information Elements, with ElementIds 434 to 454. These are the eleven mibObjectValue elements (434 to 444), the field options elements mibObjectIdentifier, mibSubIdentifier, mibIndexIndicator, mibCaptureTimeSemantics, mibContextEngineID and mibContextName (445 to 450), and the type elements mibObjectName, mibObjectDescription, mibObjectSyntax and mibModuleName (451 to 454).

The RFC also includes worked examples, such as exporting the number of established TCP connections from tcpCurrEstab, whose OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.6.9 becomes the 9-octet BER string 06072B060102010609.
sections.eli5: The official registry book got new entries so that everyone uses the same number for each kind of sticker.
